evidence: Judge agent+model: task.toml:30-35 is the exact frozen shared block (REWARDKIT_JUDGE = "claude-code", REWARDKIT_MODEL = "z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx", OpenRouter base URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}", ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = ""); lines 17-40 are byte-identical to the template. All five judge.toml [judge] blocks carry only judge = "claude-code" fallback, mode, timeout, isolated, prompt_template - no model, reasoning_effort, temperature or weight. Judge CLIs/browser: tests/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the template (diff SAME): @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.281, @openai/codex@0.151.0, @playwright/mcp@0.0.79, harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7, express@5.1.0, better-sqlite3@12.4.1; Chromium is installed via the playwright CLI nested in @playwright/mcp@0.0.79, whose registry dependencies (npm view, checked today) are exact pins playwright/playwright-core 1.63.0-alpha-2026-08-05, so the browser build is transitively pinned and symlinked to /usr/local/bin/chromium, which every judge.toml's playwright-mcp args reference. Shared tools: tests/tools/score.py, restart_mcp.py and tests/test.sh are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff SAME). Fixed clock: no graded rule depends on the calendar date. The only graded time rule is an elapsed 15-second live-update window (instruction.md:5, hireops_rules.md section 5; functional/polish criteria e.g. scored/polish/judge.toml:23 'within 15 seconds, no reload'), which is relative wall time, not a date. Unread is defined by message counts since last open (hireops_rules.md section 6) and seeded as read_count integers (seed reads[0] = {'read_count': 120}), not timestamps; Activity 'newest first' and undo eligibility ('nobody has touched those cards since', 'until the same person has made a later one') are event-order rules. Seed timestamps (messages up to 2026-07-29T11:15:00Z, notes 2026-07-20/22) only drive display; the golden orders by autoincrement id (solution/app/src/index.js:158,166,189) and uses new Date() only to stamp new records (index.js:59). So no fixed clock is needed and none is missing. Open verifier network ([verifier.environment] network_mode = "public") is correct per profile and row text. Raw evidence: hashes for qc/repairs/hireops-2026-10-03-workspace/workspace.cjs (7bbf898f...) and results/workspace.json (8d72fd13...) match the index; its scope states the golden script ran in a locally built verifier image (hireops-verifier:20261002-permission-repair), not a configured judge run - not needed for this static pinning row. Counterexamples tried: (a) a broken app cannot exploit the clock because there is no date-based grading; (b) a conforming app that timestamps with its own clock or orders Activity by created_at at second resolution could tie two actions in the same second - a latent ambiguity of the app's design, not a verifier nondeterminism, and judge actions are normally seconds apart (P3 observation only). Residual items that are not defects under this row's text: base images pinned by tag not digest and apt packages unpinned (template-controlled, check-dockerfiles treats unpinned apt as NOTE); LLM judge sampling is inherently stochastic and the row explicitly does not require temperature or prompt-version markers; run-to-run judge variance is unmeasured.
